subject.title: fix(openclaw): prevent private state races during publication

question: Should Crabline permanently reject existing OpenClaw private-state ancestry or mutation claims that cannot prove current-user POSIX ownership or owner-only Windows ACLs, even when an upgraded installation then fails closed?
rationale: The patch deliberately tightens a filesystem trust boundary and can stop existing setups; automated tests cannot determine whether that compatibility tradeoff is the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Adopt strict ownership
options.body: Require verified current-user ownership or owner-only ACLs and accept explicit failures for nonconforming private-state paths.

options.title: Add legacy migration
options.body: Safely repair attributable legacy paths before enforcing the stricter boundary, with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause the hardening
options.body: Retain current behavior until maintainers narrow the cross-platform ownership and migration contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict ownership
recommendation.body: Require verified current-user ownership or owner-only ACLs and accept explicit failures for nonconforming private-state paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This repository member is the only concrete recent contributor identified across the proposed trust-boundary implementation.
